candidates.title: Planet Opens New Berlin Manufacturing Facility for Pelican Build-Out
candidates.raw_excerpt: Planet officially opened its new Berlin manufacturing facility on Tuesday, marking facility handover and cleanroom fit-out. The 5,700-square-meter facility, announced last year to double Pelican satellite production capacity, is expected to begin production this fall. It’s a key part of Planet’s expansion in Germany, which has been the company’s base in Europe for 10 years. Planet aims to meet growing demand from the European market and hire 70 new employees in addition to the company’s 150 employees in Berlin already. “When you couple [Planet] being there for a decade [with] the largest economy in Europe, needing to re-industrialize the space ecosystem, the tech talent there is phenomena in optics, signals processing, and Earth Observation — that it was the natural step for us to just expand that office and add a factory,” Planet co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Robbie Schingler told Via Satellite last week during World Space Business Week. Ahead of the factory opening, Planet recently signed a deal to launch the first Pelican satellite built in Germany with Isar Aerospace on a German-built rocket. The launch itself will take place from the Andøya Space complex in Norway. Isar Aerospace just had success with its second launch, another piece of momentum for Germany’s space industry. The Planet/Isar launch is expected in early 2027. Planet has longstanding German customers and partners including the German Federal Agency for Cartography and Geodesy (BKG). Schingler noted that Planet looks to support Spock-2, a Bundeswehr planned multi-sensor imaging and sensing satellite constellation. “We hope to be central to the coalition to support Germany to have their own eyes, and to be able to also serve other European customers that want much more of a European space ecosystem, so that they could they could choose to purchase satellites from our German factory,” Schingler added. candidates.raw_excerpt: Eutelsat tested OneWeb Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) connectivity in Poland for the first time in a recent demonstration on PKP Intercity ’s live rail network with a Kymeta terminal. candidates.title: TRL11 Will Build Imaging Tech for SR-1 Freedom
candidates.raw_excerpt: TRL11 has received a NASA contract to provide imaging systems for the Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom mission to Mars. “It will be the first time a camera we built travels to another planet and captures images of it,” TRL11 CEO Nicolaas Verheem said in a statement.  Freedom isn’t free: The $2B SR-1 mission is expected to launch in late 2028 to Mars as the first fission-powered interplanetary spacecraft. NASA first announced SR-1 at the space agency’s Ignition event in March. In addition to demoing how nuclear tech can help with interplanetary deep space travel, SR-1 will deliver a trio of SkyFall helicopters to Mars to conduct advance work for future crewed missions to the red planet. What’s onboard: TRL11 will build space cameras and edge computing systems for SR-1, according to a press release. That hardware will enable NASA to capture, process, and store high-res imagery of the mission—including the moment SkyFall deploys to Mars—and ensure the photos can be sent back to Earth. NASA is also considering adding more of TRL11’s tech to the mission, according to a press release, including: VIPLink comms system; VIP1st software to prioritize downloads; Commander software to manage spacecraft imaging. Teamwork makes the dream work: TRL11 isn’t the only company contributing to the Martian mission. AeroVironment is co-designing and co-manufacturing the SkyFall helos, in partnership with JPL. candidates.raw_excerpt:
As the world's two leading AI powers, China and the United States cannot afford to let dialogue lapse even amid competition. While they have recently differed over model distillation, that dispute is not the core issue in their AI relationship.

Distillation is a well-established, general-purpose technique – "knowledge refinement," as Gai Keke of Zhongguancun Academy puts it. AI companies worldwide, Chinese and American alike, use it to optimize models and improve efficiency. Its essence is catching up, not surpassing; it creates no original breakthroughs out of thin air. Even OpenAI's Dean Ball says distillation is not the main driver of China's recent AI advances.

If distillation isn't the core issue, what is? Both Chinese and US experts agree: Sharing risks, jointly building rules and jointly governing should top the agenda – because when it comes to AI safety, danger knows no borders.

candidates.raw_excerpt: The final ViaSat-3 satellite entered service late last week, completing deployment of Viasat’s high-capacity satellite trio. This satellite, ViaSat-3 F2, was actually the second satellite to launch, and it launched in November of last year . All three satellites are now in service and the ViaSat-3 constellation is fully operational after the F3 satellite entered service about a month ago in late August . The F3 satellite covers the Asia-Pacific region and F2 covers the Americas. Each satellite adds more than 1 terabit per second of capacity to Viasat’s network to bolster its business in aviation, maritime, government, and broadband. The F1 satellite, which launched in 2023, suffered an anomaly with its antenna deployment. That satellite is operational, but only delivering a fraction of the capacity that was expected. Beyond the capacity, the satellites are equipped with beamforming technology to allocate beams based on the location of demand, which Viasat sees as a critical differentiator. “We believe that the VS3 satellites are the most advanced commercial satellites in the world in terms of adaptive beam forming for cost efficiencies, user performance improvements that offer higher speeds on both forward and return links, and resilience to interference,” Viasat CEO Mark Dankberg said in a statement. “We also believe VS3 technology sets new commercial standards for solar power generation and thermal dissipation – both critical technology challenges for developing economical data centers in space.” The post Final ViaSat-3 Satellite Enters Service, Completing High-Capacity Trio appeared first on Via Satellite .

candidates.title: Intellian to Develop Multi-Band WGS Terminals With Network Innovations
candidates.raw_excerpt: Intellian Technologies and Network Innovations plan to jointly develop and distribute multi-band Wideband Global Satcom (WGS) flyaway terminals for military and government customers under a new strategic partnership announced last week. This will be Intellian’s first tactical ground WGS flyaway platform. Intellian said these terminals are set to be the first to support simultaneous Mil-X, Mil Ka-band and commercial Ka- and Ku-band connectivity. The platform is designed for multi-band and multi-orbit operations across Low-Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium-Earth Orbit (MEO), Geostationary Orbit (GEO), and Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO), as well as interoperability with emerging satellite networks. Network Innovations provides managed network services and system integration and has an established military and government market presence. The two companies have worked together for many years and this is a new multi-year agreement to expand their relationship. Intellian CEO Eric Sung said it marks an expansion of the company’s military-government portfolio. “By combining simultaneous X-band and Military Ka-band capability, access to wider commercial Ka frequencies, and multi-orbit connectivity in a rapidly deployable architecture, we are addressing the increasingly complex communications requirements of modern defense operations. Our goal is to give operators greater flexibility, resilience, and assured connectivity wherever their missions take them,” Sung said in a release. In March, Intellian previewed it would be moving into WGS flyaway terminals during SATShow Week. Flyaway terminals are meant to be rapidly deployable for forces in the field, to be set up in less than 30 minutes. Intellian also said it plans to expand the platform for government, enterprise, and critical communications applications outside of military. candidates.raw_excerpt:
The linear accelerator of the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) successfully generated and delivered an electron beam on Sunday, marking a key step forward in the construction of the world's most advanced fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility in the low-energy range.

Located in Hefei, capital city of east China's Anhui Province, the institution is a fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility operating at a designed energy of 2.2 gigaelectronvolts (GeV) and based on diffraction-limited storage ring technology. It is also a major national science and technology infrastructure project in China.

By generating highly intense and coherent light, the facility will serve as a "super microscope" for scientists to probe the microscopic structure of matter.

Compared with third-generation synchrotron radiation sources, HALF is expected to produce soft X-rays with more than 100 times higher brightness and coherence. It will enable the development of experimental techniques with greater precision and sensitivity in the spatial, temporal and energy domains, providing an important research platform for studying microscopic particle behavior, the structure of light elements and changes in the electronic, chemical and spin states of materials.

candidates.raw_excerpt:
Known as the "Oriental gem" and an ecological barometer, the crested ibis is highly sensitive to changes in its habitat. On Sunday, 20 crested ibises were released into the wild at a site more than 1,500 meters above sea level in the Xiaolongshan forest area in northwest China's Gansu Province, marking the westernmost and highest-altitude crested ibis rewilding effort in China to date.

The release also marks a new stage in Gansu's conservation efforts, as the province moves from captive breeding toward rebuilding a wild population.

Before the release, the birds spent more than 20 days in an acclimatization enclosure about 7 kilometers from their breeding facility. Surrounded by trees and located next to shallow wetlands, the enclosure was designed to provide a gradual transition to the natural environment.

The birds were allowed to leave at their own pace. Staff gradually opened the enclosure's gates, but did not force the birds to fly out. Some may initially remain inside and observe their surroundings, which is normal after years in captivity.

candidates.raw_excerpt: Using NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, a team of scientists has discovered the largest, newly formed crater ever found in the solar system. Identified during a routine data-quality check as a bright spot with a dark halo, the discovery highlights the ever-changing landscape of our celestial neighbor. “I just stopped, dropped everything, and started looking into what that spot was,” said Robert Wagner, an image-processing specialist from Intuitive Machines, who first identified the crater when working with Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) data. By comparing new imagery of the region with old imagery, Wagner confirmed that a new crater had formed. Analysis of Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) data shows that the crater formed between April 11 and May 22, 2024, along the Moon’s eastern edge. The size of the crater suggests that the culprit — likely a comet or asteroid — was roughly the size of a three- to six-story building. The crater has officially been named McGetchin Crater after lunar scientist Tom McGetchin. Before (right) and after (left) wide-angle image of the area surrounding McGetchin. The new crater is circled in the left image. (Credit: NASA Goddard/Intuitive Machines/Robert Wagner) The crater itself measures approximately 222 m wide and 43 m deep, spanning more than two American football fields in length and three vertically stacked yellow school buses in depth. Scientists estimate new craters this size to appear once every century.
